claims.old: An inner control loop samples at one rate, an outer loop at another, and a receiver at a third.
claims.new: An inner control loop samples at one rate, an outer loop at another, and a receiver at a third.

claims.old: #### The base grid, and the pair every rate compiles to
claims.new: #### The base grid and the gate

claims.old: Rule. Every discrete component's period is an integer multiple of a base tick period `Δt_base`.
claims.new: Every discrete component's period is an integer multiple of a base tick period `Δt_base` (D-019).

claims.old: `Δt_base` is itself an integer multiple of the continuous step, with `N_base` steps per base tick ($\Delta t_{\mathrm{base}} = N_{\mathrm{base}} \cdot h$, $N_{\mathrm{base}} \ge 1$).
claims.new: `Δt_base` is itself an integer multiple of the continuous step, with `N_base` steps per base tick ($\Delta t_{\mathrm{base}} = N_{\mathrm{base}} \cdot h$, $N_{\mathrm{base}} \ge 1$).

claims.old: That is the harmonic grid.
claims.new: That is the harmonic grid.

claims.old: Ticks therefore land on step boundaries, which is the only place anything discrete ever happens (D-019).
claims.new: Ticks therefore land on step boundaries, which is the only place anything discrete ever happens.

claims.old: Two indices. Frames are counted by the frame index `k`.
claims.new: Frames (iterations of the loop) are counted by the frame index `k`.

claims.old: The frame top at `t = k·h` is a base tick exactly when `k` is a multiple of `N_base`.
claims.new: The frame top at `t = t₀ + k·h` is a base tick exactly when `k` is a multiple of `N_base`.

claims.old: Its tick index is then `tick = k ÷ N_base`.
claims.new: Its tick index is then `tick = k ÷ N_base`.

claims.old: A frame top that is no base tick has no tick index, and neither does a `t` boundary.
claims.new: A frame top that is no base tick has no tick index, and neither does a boundary at a localized event time `t` (§10.4, D-185).

claims.old: One pair per component. However an author declares a rate, and however deeply the declaration is nested, the build compiles it to two integers per discrete component.
claims.new: However an author declares a rate, and however deeply the declaration is nested, the build compiles it to two integers per discrete component (D-185).

claims.old: The divisor `D` is the component's period in base ticks.
claims.new: The divisor `D` is the component's period in base ticks.

claims.old: The phase `Φ` is its offset in base ticks.
claims.new: The phase `Φ` is its offset in base ticks.

claims.old: The pair is kept in the canonical residue `0 ≤ Φ < D`, so the component's ticks fall at base-tick indices `Φ`, `Φ + D`, `Φ + 2D`, and so on.
claims.new: The pair is kept in the canonical residue `0 ≤ Φ < D`, so the component's ticks fall at base-tick indices `Φ`, `Φ + D`, `Φ + 2D`, and so on.

claims.old: The gate. A component is due at a boundary when `(tick − Φ) % D == 0`, where `tick` is the boundary's tick index.
claims.new: A component is due at a boundary when `(tick − Φ) % D == 0`, where `tick` is the boundary's tick index (D-185).

claims.old: That subtraction and remainder are the whole admission test.
claims.new: That subtraction and remainder are the whole admission test.

claims.old: It costs one subtraction more than a phase-free test would, over a lattice fixed at build time.
claims.new: It costs one subtraction more than a phase-free test would, over a lattice fixed at build time.

claims.old: #### Discrete stages run only at their own ticks
claims.new: #### Zero-order hold and the two sweep variants

claims.old: Rule. A discrete component's `y_state`/`y_direct` run only at its own ticks.
claims.new: A discrete component's `y_state`/`y_direct` run only at its own ticks (D-019).

claims.old: Its cells hold in between.
claims.new: Its cells (its entries in the signal table) hold in between.

claims.old: This is zero-order hold (ZOH), stated in sweep terms.
claims.new: This is zero-order hold (ZOH), stated in sweep terms.

claims.old: Why. Re-running a discrete component's stages at every boundary would un-sample a sampled-data controller (D-019).
claims.new: The reason for the hold is that re-running a discrete component's stages at every boundary would un-sample a sampled-data controller.

claims.old: Delivering that hold takes two statically distinct sweep variants, compiled from one entry list.
claims.new: Delivering that hold takes two statically distinct sweep variants, compiled from one entry list (D-147).

claims.old: Discreteness is a build-time fact, so the split is static rather than a runtime test (D-147).
claims.new: Discreteness is a build-time fact, so the split is static rather than a runtime test.

claims.old: The interior sweep walks continuous entries only.
claims.new: The interior sweep walks continuous entries only (D-147).

claims.old: RK stage evaluations (§10.3) and localization guard trial evaluations (§10.4) run this variant.
claims.new: RK stage evaluations (§10.3) and localization guard trial evaluations (§10.4) run this variant.

claims.old: The ZOH therefore holds mid-step by construction.
claims.new: The ZOH therefore holds mid-step by construction.

claims.new: Discrete entries are not gated out at runtime.

claims.old: They are absent from the walk at compile time, so the hot path carries no gating test at all.
claims.new: They are absent from the walk at compile time, so the hot path carries no gating test at all.

claims.old: The boundary sweep walks the full list, with discrete entries gated by `(tick − Φ) % D` against the boundary's tick index.
claims.new: The boundary sweep walks the full list, with discrete entries gated by `(tick − Φ) % D` against the boundary's tick index (D-147).

claims.old: It is the variant the §10.6 macro-sequence runs.
claims.new: It is the variant the §10.6 macro-sequence runs.

claims.old: It is not one fixed list either, because different boundaries run different subsets of the execution order.
claims.new: It is not one fixed list either, because different boundaries run different subsets of the execution order.

claims.old: The split applies to both sweep blocks.
claims.new: The split applies to both sweep blocks (D-147).

claims.old: The discrete tier's `y_state` entries are absent from the interior stage-1 walk, exactly as its `y_direct` entries are absent from the interior stage-2 walk.
claims.new: The discrete tier's `y_state` entries are absent from the interior stage-1 walk, exactly as its `y_direct` entries are absent from the interior stage-2 walk.

claims.old: #### The due set is a property of the boundary
claims.new: #### Due sets

claims.old: Rule. The due set is computed once for the boundary and reused by every re-sweep of its quiescence iteration (the fixed point where a round of handlers fires nothing, §10.6).
claims.new: The due set is computed once for the boundary and reused by every re-sweep of its quiescence iteration (D-147). Quiescence is the fixed point where a round of handlers fires nothing (§10.6).

claims.old: It is a property of the boundary, not of the sweep call.
claims.new: The due set is a property of the boundary, not of the sweep call.

claims.old: Why. A due component is at its tick instant for the whole boundary, not for one round of it.
claims.new: That holds because a due component is at its tick instant for the whole boundary, not for one round of it.

claims.new: Each kind of boundary has its own due set:

claims.old: At a tick frame top (every `N_base`-th frame top), the due set is every discrete component whose gate admits the tick index.
claims.new: At a tick frame top (every `N_base`-th frame top), the due set is every discrete component whose gate admits the tick index.

claims.old: These are the `(D, Φ)` pairs with `(tick − Φ) % D == 0`.
claims.new: These are the `(D, Φ)` pairs with `(tick − Φ) % D == 0`.

claims.old: At an off-tick frame top (a frame top with `N_base > 1` that is no base tick), the due set is empty.
claims.new: At an off-tick frame top (a frame top with `N_base > 1` that is no base tick), the due set is empty.

claims.old: The tick counter has not advanced, so no component is at a tick instant.
claims.new: The tick counter has not advanced, so no component is at a tick instant.

claims.old: At a `t` boundary, the due set is empty for the same reason.
claims.new: At a `t` boundary, the due set is empty for the same reason.

claims.new: A modulo test against the unadvanced index would wrongly re-admit the previous tick's due set.

claims.new: At boundary zero (the initialization boundary, which runs the ordinary macro-sequence with an empty integrate), the due set is everything with `Φ = 0` (D-185, D-205).

claims.new: At tick index 0 the gate reads `(0 − Φ) % D == 0`.
